demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson's dispatch runs the live gate on the candidate it makes, and the gate asks acme's golden rows; run it as lesson 4.3 ran its gate, with acme on the kit's own index, and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

steps.expected:
# documind-cd.yml reads 4 repository variables. Set them on YOUR-GITHUB-USER/YOUR-REPO, the repository wif.tf trusts:
gh variable set GCP_PROJECT --repo YOUR-GITHUB-USER/YOUR-REPO --body documind-ai-YOUR-ID
gh variable set GCP_REGION --repo YOUR-GITHUB-USER/YOUR-REPO --body asia-south1
gh variable set WIF_PROVIDER --repo YOUR-GITHUB-USER/YOUR-REPO --body projects/NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/documind-github/providers/github-oidc
gh variable set CICD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT --repo YOUR-GITHUB-USER/YOUR-REPO --body sa-documind-cicd@documind-ai-YOUR-ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# The trust (wif.tf): YOUR-GITHUB-USER/YOUR-REPO, id REPO_ID, ref refs/heads/main. A run from any other ref is refused at the auth step.
# Dispatch from that branch, on the candidate path - path=clouddeploy would replace documind-api's settings with run-service.yaml's:
#   gh workflow run documind-cd.yml --repo YOUR-GITHUB-USER/YOUR-REPO --ref main -f path=candidate
WARNING: YOUR-GITHUB-USER/YOUR-REPO has no production environment, or gh's account cannot see the repository. GitHub creates the environment the first time a job names it, with no required reviewer, and promote would then move traffic with nobody approving. Create it with a reviewer before the first dispatch: Settings > Environments > production > Required reviewers (on a private repository, required reviewers need a paid GitHub plan)

demos.heading: What may stop the first dispatch, the trust that cannot move, and the path without GitHub
demos.purpose: The workflow's two release steps are make targets, and you can run them from the operator shell as yourself: the same image built by Cloud Build, the same revision with no traffic and the tag candidate. It proves the build and the deploy, not the keyless identity, because your own sign-in makes both calls. It also moves the candidate tag to the revision it makes, so run it only if step 6 could not run.
